Can countries double energy efficiency while electricity demand accelerates?

With electricity demand expected to grow 3.6% annually through 2030, driven by digitalization, AI, cooling, and electrification, efficiency is one of the fastest ways to reduce energy system costs. Global efficiency-related investment is set to reach almost USD 800 billion in 2025, over 70% since 2015.

The UAE Consensus commits countries to tripling renewables and doubling efficiency improvement rates to around 4% annually by 2030. Yet gains were only 1% in 2024 and are projected to reach just 1.8% in 2025.

Efficiency is an opportunity for the Global South. It reduces exposure to volatile electricity prices and has already avoided the need for 20% more fossil fuel imports. 

Since 2000, efficiency improvements have cut household energy bills in advanced economies by up to 20%, while industries now produce 20% more value per unit of energy than in 2000. 

Three coordinated areas can accelerate energy efficiency implementation solutions:

⚡ Strengthen national efficiency frameworks
Embedding efficiency targets into digital, industrial, and affordability policies is critical to reach the required 4% annual improvement rate. Brazil’s Artificial Intelligence Plan allocates over $900 million to support sustainable energy systems for data centers and AI infrastructure, demonstrating how digital strategies can align with national efficiency and decarbonization pathways.

💻 Reduce cooling demand for datacenters and digital infrastructure intensity 
Cooling systems account for between 7% of total electricity consumption in highly efficient hyperscale data centres and over 30% in less-efficient enterprise facilities.

📊 Deploy AI for system-wide optimization
AI can map infrastructure gaps, anticipate demand, and optimize energy flows in real time. AI is estimated to contribute up to 5.4 GtCO2e in annual emissions reductions by 2035 through accelerating low-carbon transitions across sectors.

UNDP is supporting countries in aligning digital transformation with energy efficiency—integrating governance frameworks, smart infrastructure, and system optimization with sustainable development goals.

As electricity systems expand, efficiency must scale alongside demand to prevent rising costs, system strain, and stalled development progress.
